# d3tools documentation conventions

## Two tiers

Rule: if it can be expressed in the workflow JSON, environment variables, the CLI
(`scripts/run_workflow.py`) or `WorkflowDefinition.load()` / `wf.run()`, it belongs in the
**User Guide** (`docs/user-guide/`). If it requires writing Python against d3tools classes,
it belongs in the **Developer Guide** (`docs/developer/`).

- Each fact has exactly one owning page. The other tier links to it, never copies it.
- A User Guide page must be understandable without opening any Developer page.
- Example: dataset `fallback` (configurable in JSON) is User Guide; `set_parents()`
  (Python only, used internally by dryes) is Developer Guide.
- The API reference in `docs/developer/reference/` is generated by mkdocstrings from
  docstrings. Never hand-write function signatures there; fix the docstring instead.

## Topics

Work is split by topic. Existing pages that serve as source material for each topic:

| Topic | Existing pages |
|-------|----------------|
| configuration | `docs/configuration/overview.md`, `tags.md`, `environment.md` |
| workflow-sections | `docs/configuration/workflow-sections.md` |
| datasets | `docs/configuration/datasets.md`, `docs/datasets/*.md` |
| timestepping | `docs/timestepping.md` |
| logging | `docs/logging/*.md` |
| thumbnails | `docs/thumbnails/overview.md` |
| notification | none yet (feature is EXPERIMENTAL, email sending known broken) |
| getting-started | `docs/getting-started.md`, `docs/index.md`, `docs/examples/*.md` |

## Truth and verification

- Ground truth is `src/d3tools/` and `tests/`, in that order. Never `build/` (stale copy).
- Every behavioural claim must be traceable to code or a test. If you can't find it, don't
  write it; if it exists in code but has no test, say so ("not covered by tests").
- Run checks with the shared venv:
  `/home/luca/Documents/CIMA_code/workspace_env/.venv/bin/python scripts/check_docs.py <files>`
  (run from the `d3tools/` folder).
- JSON blocks must be valid JSON. Complete workflow snippets are parsed by the checker, so
  they must actually parse. For intentionally partial snippets (`"..."` placeholders), put
  `<!-- check-docs: skip -->` on the line directly before the fence.
- No `//` comments inside JSON blocks.

## Style

The gold standard is `docs/thumbnails/overview.md`:
- short intro saying what the feature is and where it lives in the package;
- tables for keys/parameters with Required / Type / Default / Description;
- exact rules (ordering, edge cases, error types and messages) instead of vague prose;
- small, realistic examples; no marketing language, no emojis, no ✅/❌ blocks.

## Known facts (verified)

- Top-level keys: `workflow_name, tags, datasets, env, workflow_log, workflow_sections,
  exec_options, engine, other_options`. No `name`, no `time`.
- Sections run sequentially. There is no parallel execution.
- Dataset refs: `{x}` always resolves; `{datasets.x}` / `{DATASETS.x}` only if the prefix
  matches the literal key case. Unresolved refs silently stay strings.
- Email notification is experimental: document it as such, do not document it as working.
